thread:
priya_sales: FYI - QuantumEdge wants a Private/VPC POC. They have strict netsec: must preserve L3 source IPs for IDS, require mTLS to the connector, and only want a very small set of firewall openings. Also asking if PrivateLink vs TGW peering changes cost or SLA. Need quick guidance and an allowlist they can hand to security.

sam_se: Topline: mTLS supported. L3 preservation only with direct routing (peering/TGW) or an IP-preserve passthrough mode; PrivateLink will NAT to the connector ENI by default. If they can accept X-Forwarded-For it's easiest, but you mentioned IDS needs L3 so probably not.

alex_net: Agreed. Options and tradeoffs:
- PrivateLink (interface endpoint) -> minimal surface area, DNS-based or ENI IP allowlist. Easiest for locked-down VPCs. Source IP becomes our connector ENI/NAT.
- VPC Peering / Transit Gateway -> preserves source IPs, but requires route table changes, symmetric routing, and security group updates. More operational overhead and broader network exposure.
- IP-preserve proxy -> advanced pattern where connector does zero SNAT, relies on transit/TGW. Requires us and customer to coordinate ASNs/BGP for failover.

juan_platform: Pricing impact: managed static egress IPs (NAT or managed EIP pool) are an add-on for Private deployments: one-time setup + per-EIP monthly + small per-GB egress surcharge. Transit Gateway peering can incur AWS TGW data transfer costs on their side. Dedicated reserved capacity can include static IPs as part of the bundle at a discount.

priya_sales: They explicitly reject app-layer headers for audit. So we need to plan for peering or TGW. Can we still demo anything quickly?

alex_net: Quick demo path: 1) Provision PrivateLink and provide static test EIPs for allowlist so their firewall folks can try connectivity and run functional tests (mTLS health checks). 2) Parallel design for peering/TGW to achieve L3 preservation; this is phase 2 and needs netops coordination + route planning. Demo will prove app functionality while design work proceeds.

sam_se: Minimal firewall checklist to hand to their team (confirm final EIPs with infra):
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 18.204.77.111, 18.204.77.112 (test ENIs)
- Allow outbound TCP 8443 to: 18.204.77.113 (management plane, optional)
- Allow DNS UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver or allowed DNS IP
- Allow NTP UDP 123 for cert time sync
- Allow ephemeral return ports 1024-65535 if using NAT
- Allow ICMP type 3 and 4 for PMTU discovery
```

juan_platform: Also call out MTU and MSS clamp guidance: many SD-WAN devices MTU=1400 or less. If they see TLS issues, test MTU with `ping -M do -s 1400 <peer-ip>` and enable MSS clamp on firewall for TCP to avoid fragmentation.

priya_sales: Can we provide test certs and a curl snippet they can run?

sam_se: Yes, we'll provide short-lived mTLS certs for the POC. Example mTLS curl (replace certs):
```bash
curl --cert poc-client.crt --key poc-client.key -v https://quantum.pvtl.redwood.ai:443/healthz
```
Non-mTLS quick test: `curl -v https://quantum.pvtl.redwood.ai:443/healthz`

alex_net: For L3-preserve peering checklist (high level):
- Agree on CIDR allocations (avoid overlap) and route propagation rules
- Update route tables -> route customer subnets to our peering attachment / TGW
- Security groups: allow ingress from customer CIDR to connector ports (443, 8443)
- Disable SNAT on connector path so client src IPs are preserved
- Plan for failover: ensure return path to our ASN and BGP session parameters if using TGW/BGP

infra-bot: maintenance notice: infra provisioning freeze 2025-07-04 23:00 - 2025-07-05 05:00 UTC may delay ENI creation if requested then.

juan_platform: Security questionnaire quick answers for the form:
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments; HSM option available under EAA.
- Audit logs: request metadata (no payloads) can be exported to S3/CloudWatch with configurable retention; payload logging can be disabled for compliance.
- SOC2: we provide SOC2 type II upon NDA/enterprise pack.
- TLS inspection: we do not perform TLS interception on customer traffic; mutual TLS supported.

priya_sales: Timeline: Customer wants a working connectivity test by Thursday. Can we get test EIPs + certs by Wednesday EOD?

alex_net: I'll request test ENIs/EIPs from infra and generate certs. Need a primary contact for their firewall team (name + egress IPs).

priya_sales: Contact is 'david.netsec@quantumedge.com' - I'll loop him in.

sam_se: I'll prepare a short troubleshooting checklist for their team (packet capture pointers, tcpdump filters, check for MTU/TLS SNI mismatch, confirm client cert CN).

juan_platform: I'll assemble a short pricing note and attach it to the POC SOW: include one-time set up, monthly EIP fee, per-GB surcharge, and discount if they commit to 12mo reserved capacity.

priya_sales: Great. Plan: 1) Alex -> EIPs + certs by Wed EOD, 2) Sam -> test scripts + troubleshoot tips by Wed EOD, 3) Juan -> pricing note by tomorrow morning. I'll intro David once EIPs are ready. Any blockers?

alex_net: No blockers other than infra window; will aim to provision before freeze.

priya_sales: Thanks team :heart:
